subject: Prod severity: sustained latency & 500s — reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@blueharbor.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+prod@blueharbor.ai
Date: 2027-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: high latency & 500s spike (BlueHarbor)

Hi Hannah / Naomi —

We started seeing a jump in 95th/99th percentile latency at ~08:45 PT and a wave of 500s from the endpoint backed by our dedicated GPU pool. Impact: live user workflows stalled for ~11 minutes, ~14% request error rate during the window.

Attached a sample of traces and a short query dump (query-sample.jsonl). The customer policy is on reserved capacity and they expect predictable throughput — this is causing operational and legal friction on their side.

What we need: fast triage, confirmation whether this is a platform-side capacity issue or a customer-side workload change, and whether you can authorize temporary burst capacity while we stabilize. We also need a note for our execs — BlueHarbor is on a Q4 launch.

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
CTO, BlueHarbor AI

--
Attachment: query-sample.jsonl (samples of the failing requests)

Subject: Re: Production: high latency & 500s spike (BlueHarbor)

Alex — thank you for the quick flag and sample.

High level: I'm standing up an incident loop with engineering and capacity ops. Naomi, can you pull the dedicated pool headroom/queue depth and reserved throughput utilization for the last 60 minutes? David, please start a lightweight trace to check the KV-cache hit rate and sequence-length distribution for BlueHarbor tenant.

Short asks for BlueHarbor while we triage:
- Can you confirm if any model switch, prompt template change, or batch job started at ~08:30 PT?
- If possible, reduce max-seq on non-critical requests to 512 for the next 20 minutes (helps reduce long tail).

I'll escalate to Jonas for a quick exec-level approval if we need to authorize a temporary burst or emergency override on reserved throughput. I'll keep you posted every 15 minutes.

-Hannah

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Alex Moreno <alex@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: high latency & 500s spike (BlueHarbor)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed: Dedicated GPU pool serving BlueHarbor hit sustained queue depth ~4.5x above baseline between 08:40-08:56 PT. Token throughput plateaued while tail latency climbed.
- Root signal: a small set of unusually long sequences (several >4k tokens) combined with a high KV-cache miss rate produced a CPU-side scheduling stall that spilled requests into the backpressure path. This manifested as 502/500 for requests that timed out the request router.
- Why reserved didn't auto-scale: their reserved-policy is capped by the committed throughput profile (DH-5482). Overflow routing is rate-limited by the current allocation rules; autoscale to shared capacity is only allowed when pool headroom >15% (policy decision). During the spike headroom dipped below that threshold.

Immediate mitigations I executed (10:00 PT):
- Enabled short-term preemptive eviction on large KV entries for BlueHarbor tenant to reduce cache footprint.
- Deployed a routing rule to preferentially route non-critical requests to a cheaper, quantized model variant (gen-small-q4f).
- Opened a request for 60-minute burst uplift of +30% reserved throughput to the ops plane (pending exec approval).

Next steps / asks:
- Sales / AM approval required to authorize the burst (cost/credit implications noted below).
- We should run a quick prompt/seq audit on BlueHarbor side; Alex, if you can confirm any workload shifts that created those long sequences that will help.

Preliminary impact estimate: the one-hour burst (+30%) will reduce queue depth to baseline within ~8-12 minutes and drop 95th latency back to normal. Estimated incremental cost: $1.8k for the hour; recommend offering a partial credit as goodwill if we confirm platform root cause.

Logs & evidence: attached short-term-mitigation-checklist.md and links to traces in the incident dashboard.

-David
David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-10-10T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: high latency & 500s spike (BlueHarbor) — authorization

Thanks team — and Alex, apologies for the disruption. We need to both stop the customer impact quickly and document decisions for the account/review.

Decision: I approve a one-hour burst +30% on BlueHarbor's reserved throughput effective immediately. Operations: please apply the burst now and monitor the queue depth and 95th/99th latency.

Commercial note (for Hannah): please offer BlueHarbor a 50% credit on the incremental burst cost while we complete RCA and determine any platform remediation. Finance sign-off not required for this goodwill credit; track in the DH-5482 deal notes.

Engineering asks: David, continue the KV-cache eviction check and follow up with an RCA doc that includes:
- exact request sequences that triggered >2k token churn
- whether model weights/compilation path triggered inefficient kernels for those sequences
- suggested platform policy change (short-term: lower overflow threshold to 10% headroom; medium-term: adaptive overflow that considers sequence-length distribution)

I'll join the post-incident readout at 15:30 PT. Hannah — please confirm with Alex that the immediate impact is resolved and send a brief note to their execs summarizing the actions and the credit.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability & Operations
Redwood Inference
